question: According to the manual, air brakes are really three different braking systems. Which three?
choice_a: Front brake, rear brake, and trailer brake
choice_b: Primary brake, secondary brake, and auxiliary brake
choice_c: Hydraulic brake, spring brake, and disc brake
choice_d: Service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake
explanation: The manual states that air brakes are really three different braking systems: service brake, parking brake, and emergency brake, with the emergency brake system using parts of the service and parking brake systems to stop the vehicle in a brake system failure.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: According to the manual, at approximately what pressure does the governor stop the air compressor from pumping air ("cut-out"), and at what pressure does it allow pumping to resume ("cut-in")?
choice_a: Cut-out around 125 psi, cut-in around 100 psi
choice_b: Cut-out around 90 psi, cut-in around 70 psi
choice_c: Cut-out around 60 psi, cut-in around 40 psi
choice_d: Cut-out around 200 psi, cut-in around 150 psi
explanation: The manual states that when air tank pressure rises to the "cut-out" level (around 125 psi), the governor stops the compressor from pumping air; when the pressure falls to the "cut-in" pressure (around 100 psi), the governor allows the compressor to start pumping again.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: Why does the manual say it is important to drain water and oil from air tanks?
choice_a: Water and oil have no effect on the brakes
choice_b: Water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure
choice_c: It prevents the tanks from rusting on the outside only
choice_d: It is only necessary to improve fuel economy
explanation: The manual explains that compressed air usually has some water and compressor oil in it, which is bad for the air brake system; water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure, so tanks must be drained completely, either manually or via automatic drain valves.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-1

question: According to the manual, the safety relief valve installed in the first air tank is usually set to open at approximately what pressure?
choice_a: 200 psi
choice_b: 150 psi
choice_c: 125 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: The manual states a safety relief valve is installed in the first tank the air compressor pumps air to, protecting the tank and system from too much pressure, and is usually set to open at 150 psi; if it releases air, something is wrong and a mechanic should fix it.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: In an s-cam drum brake, what happens when you push the brake pedal?
choice_a: Hydraulic fluid pushes the shoes against the drum
choice_b: A power screw clamps the disc directly, bypassing the brake chamber
choice_c: Air is let into each brake chamber, moving the slack adjuster and twisting the camshaft so the s-cam forces the brake shoes against the drum
choice_d: A wedge is driven directly between the brake shoes without using air pressure
explanation: The manual describes that when you push the brake pedal, air is let into each brake chamber, air pressure pushes the rod out, moving the slack adjuster and twisting the brake camshaft, turning the s-cam, which forces the brake shoes away from one another and against the inside of the brake drum.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: How does the manual describe the operation of wedge brakes?
choice_a: Compressed air directly contacts the brake drum
choice_b: The brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart against the drum
choice_c: A power screw clamps the disc between brake lining pads like a c-clamp
choice_d: An s-cam rotates to force the shoes apart
explanation: The manual states that in wedge brakes, the brake chamber push rod pushes a wedge directly between the ends of two brake shoes, shoving them apart and against the inside of the brake drum; wedge brakes may have one or two brake chambers and may be self-adjusting or require manual adjustment.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-2

question: According to the manual, a low air pressure warning signal you can see must come on before tank pressure falls below what level?
choice_a: 80 psi
choice_b: 40 psi
choice_c: 60 psi
choice_d: 100 psi
explanation: The manual states that a low air pressure warning signal is required on vehicles with air brakes, and a warning signal you can see must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

topic: Low Air Warning on Large Buses
question: According to the manual, at what pressure range is it common for large buses to have their low pressure warning devices signal?
explanation: The manual notes that on large buses it is common for the low pressure warning devices to signal at 80-85 psi.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: According to the manual, what is true of front brake limiting valves found on some vehicles made before 1975?
choice_a: They increase stopping power in the "slippery" position
choice_b: They control the rear brakes only
choice_c: They are still required equipment on all modern trucks
choice_d: They actually reduce the vehicle's stopping power, and the control should be kept in the "normal" position for normal stopping power
explanation: The manual states that although front brake limiting valves were used to reduce the chance of front wheel skids on slippery surfaces, they actually reduce the vehicle's stopping power; tests show front wheel skids from braking are not likely even on ice, so the control should be kept in the "normal" position.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: According to the manual, tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to what range?
choice_a: 60 to 80 psi
choice_b: 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi)
choice_c: 100 to 120 psi
choice_d: 5 to 10 psi
explanation: The manual states tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi), and warns drivers not to wait for the brakes to come on automatically, but to stop safely as soon as the low air warning activates.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: According to the manual, why should you avoid pushing the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on?
choice_a: It will drain the air tanks faster than normal
choice_b: The brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure
choice_c: It has no effect either way
choice_d: It will release the spring brakes automatically
explanation: The manual cautions never to push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on, because the brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and the air pressure; not all systems are designed to prevent this.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: According to the manual, what is a modulating control valve used for?
choice_a: To disconnect the trailer brakes from the tractor
choice_b: To apply the spring brakes gradually, using a dash board control handle, so a driver can control spring braking if the service brakes fail
choice_c: To control the alcohol evaporator's fill rate
choice_d: To automatically increase air tank pressure during hard braking
explanation: The manual describes a modulating control valve on the dash board that can apply the spring brakes gradually; it is spring-loaded to give a feel for braking action, letting the driver control the spring brakes if the service brakes fail. When parking with this valve, move the lever as far as it will go and lock it in place.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-3

question: According to the manual, truck tractors with air brakes built on or after which date are required to have antilock brakes?
choice_a: March 1, 1998
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: January 1, 2000
choice_d: January 1, 1990
explanation: The manual states truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, and other air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to be equipped with antilock brakes.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-4

question: According to the manual, where are ABS malfunction lamps located on a trailer?
choice_a: On the instrument panel, same as a tractor
choice_b: Only inside the trailer's cargo area
choice_c: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
choice_d: There is no requirement for trailers to have a malfunction lamp
explanation: The manual states tractors, trucks, and buses will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the instrument panel, while trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-4

topic: What ABS Does and Does Not Do
question: According to the manual, which statement about ABS is correct?
choice_a: ABS always shortens stopping distance significantly
choice_b: ABS replaces the need for normal service brakes
choice_c: ABS is an addition to normal brakes and does not decrease or increase normal braking capability; it only activates when wheels are about to lock up
choice_d: ABS applies the brakes automatically without driver input
explanation: The manual states ABS is an addition to your normal brakes; it does not decrease or increase normal braking capability, and only activates when wheels are about to lock up. It also notes ABS does not necessarily shorten stopping distance, but helps you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-4

question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, the manual says you should allow time for the compressor to build up a minimum pressure of how much in both the primary and secondary systems?
choice_a: 125 psi
choice_b: 60 psi
choice_c: 100 psi
choice_d: 80 psi
explanation: The manual states that before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, you should allow time for the air compressor to build up a minimum of 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-5

question: According to the manual, the low air pressure warning light and buzzer in a dual air system should shut off when pressure in both systems rises to a value set by the manufacturer that must be greater than:
choice_a: 60 psi
choice_b: 100 psi
choice_c: 40 psi
choice_d: 125 psi
explanation: The manual states the warning light and buzzer should shut off when air pressure in both systems rises to a value set by the manufacturer, which must be greater than 60 psi, and should come on before the air pressure drops below 60 psi in either system.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-5

question: According to the manual, when checking slack adjusters on s-cam brakes, what movement indicates the slack adjuster probably needs adjustment?
choice_a: Any visible movement at all
choice_b: If it moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it
choice_c: If it does not move at all
choice_d: If it moves less than a quarter inch
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to park on level ground, chock the wheels, release the parking brakes, and pull hard on each slack adjuster; if a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: According to the manual, what is true about manually adjusting an automatic slack adjuster to bring the pushrod stroke within legal limits?
choice_a: It fully repairs the underlying mechanical problem
choice_b: It generally masks a mechanical problem rather than fixing it, and should only be used as a temporary emergency measure
choice_c: It is required maintenance every week
choice_d: It voids the vehicle's warranty
explanation: The manual states that manual adjustment of an automatic adjuster to bring a brake pushrod stroke within legal limits is generally masking a mechanical problem and not fixing it, and should only be used as a temporary measure in an emergency; the vehicle should be taken to a repair facility as soon as possible.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: According to the manual, brake drums or discs must not have cracks longer than what portion of the width of the friction area?
choice_a: The full width
choice_b: One quarter the width
choice_c: One half the width
choice_d: Cracks are acceptable as long as they don't go all the way through
explanation: The manual states brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than one half the width of the friction area, and linings must not be loose, soaked with oil or grease, or dangerously thin.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: According to the manual, in a dual air system with the engine at operating rpm, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within approximately how long?
choice_a: 3 minutes
choice_b: 15 seconds
choice_c: 5 minutes
choice_d: 45 seconds
explanation: The manual states that when the engine is at operating rpms, the pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems (longer build times may still be safe on vehicles with larger than minimum air tanks, per manufacturer specifications).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: According to the manual's air brake inspection procedure, pumping by the air compressor should start at about what pressure and stop at about what pressure?
choice_a: Start at about 100 psi, stop at about 125 psi
choice_b: Start at about 40 psi, stop at about 70 psi
choice_c: Start at about 150 psi, stop at about 175 psi
choice_d: Start at about 60 psi, stop at about 90 psi
explanation: The manual states that when checking the air compressor governor cut-in and cut-out pressures, pumping by the air compressor should start at about 100 psi and stop at about 125 psi (checking manufacturer's specifications for the exact values).
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: With a fully-charged air system and the parking brake released, the manual says the loss rate should be less than what for a single vehicle?
choice_a: One psi in five minutes
choice_b: Two psi in one minute
choice_c: Five psi in one minute
choice_d: Ten psi in one minute
explanation: The manual states that with a fully-charged air system (typically 125 psi), engine off and parking brake released, the air pressure loss rate should be less than two psi in one minute for single vehicles and less than three psi in one minute for combination vehicles.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-7

question: With the air pressure built up to governor cutoff and the foot brake fully applied and held for one minute, the manual says the pressure should not drop more than how much for a combination vehicle?
choice_a: Four pounds
choice_b: Ten pounds
choice_c: One pound
choice_d: Two pounds
explanation: The manual states that with the air pressure built up to governor cutoff (120-140 psi), engine off, parking brake and tractor protection valve released, and the foot brake fully applied and held for one minute, the air pressure should not drop more than three pounds for a single vehicle or four pounds for a combination vehicle.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-6

question: According to the manual's final air brake check, how should you test the parking brake?
choice_a: It cannot be tested without special equipment
choice_b: Apply the parking brake only while the vehicle is on a lift
choice_c: Drive at highway speed and apply the parking brake suddenly
choice_d: Stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that it holds
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that the parking brake will hold.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-7

topic: Braking with ABS on Only the Tractor or Only the Trailer
question: According to the manual, if only the trailer has ABS, what should you do if you lose steering control or a tractor jackknife begins?
choice_a: Apply the brakes harder to regain control
choice_b: Let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so, until you gain control
choice_c: Immediately apply the parking brake
choice_d: Nothing can be done in this situation
explanation: The manual states that when only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out, but if you lose steering control or start a tractor jackknife, you should let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so, until you gain control.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

topic: Emergency Stop Exception With Full ABS
question: According to the manual, what is the one exception to the general ABS emergency stop procedure of monitoring and backing off the brakes?
choice_a: If you always drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop you can fully apply the brakes
choice_b: If it is raining, you should always use stab braking instead
choice_c: There are no exceptions under any circumstances
choice_d: If the vehicle is empty, you should never use full brake pressure
explanation: The manual states that as you slow down you should monitor your tractor and trailer and back off the brakes if safe, with one exception: if you always drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, in an emergency stop you can fully apply the brakes.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

question: How does the manual describe the "controlled braking" method for emergency stops?
choice_a: Apply the brakes all the way and release only when fully stopped
choice_b: Pump the brakes rapidly at all times
choice_c: Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small
choice_d: Never apply the brakes; rely only on engine braking
explanation: The manual describes controlled braking as applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small; if you need a larger steering adjustment or the wheels lock, release the brakes and re-apply as soon as you can.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

question: According to the manual, in the "stab braking" method, how long can it take for the wheels to start rolling again after you release the brakes?
choice_a: The wheels start rolling instantly
choice_b: Up to one second
choice_c: Up to one minute
choice_d: Up to ten seconds
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock up, and applying the brakes fully again as soon as the wheels start rolling; it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling after release, and re-applying too soon will prevent the vehicle from straightening out.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

question: According to the manual, what four factors make up total stopping distance for a vehicle with air brakes?
choice_a: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Braking Distance
choice_b: Reaction Distance + Braking Distance only
choice_c: Perception Distance + Braking Distance + Following Distance + Stopping Distance
choice_d: Speed Distance + Weight Distance + Brake Distance + Road Distance
explanation: The manual states that total stopping distance for vehicles with air brake systems is made up of four factors: Perception Distance + Reaction Distance + Brake Lag Distance + Braking Distance = Total Stopping Distance.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

question: According to the manual, about how much distance does air brake lag add at 55 mph on dry pavement, and what is the resulting total stopping distance for an average driver under good conditions?
choice_a: About 5 feet of lag distance, with total stopping distance under 100 feet
choice_b: About 100 feet of lag distance, with total stopping distance over 800 feet
choice_c: About 32 feet of lag distance, with total stopping distance over 450 feet
choice_d: Brake lag does not add any measurable distance
explanation: The manual states that the air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet, so for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, the total stopping distance at 55 mph is over 450 feet.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-8

question: According to the manual, what causes brake fade from excessive heat?
choice_a: A drop in tire pressure
choice_b: The parking brake being left engaged
choice_c: The alcohol evaporator running dry
choice_d: Chemical changes in the brake lining that reduce friction, along with expansion of the overheated brake drums
explanation: The manual explains that brake fade results from excessive heat causing chemical changes in the brake lining, which reduce friction, and causing expansion of the brake drums; as overheated drums expand, the shoes and linings must move farther to contact the drums, reducing the force of contact.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-9

topic: Proper Braking Technique on a Downgrade
question: According to the manual's example, if your "safe" speed going down a grade is 40 mph, what should you do?
choice_a: Apply the brakes to reduce speed to 35 mph, then release, repeating as needed until the end of the downgrade
choice_b: Apply the brakes only once at the top of the grade
choice_c: Shift into neutral and coast down using only the brakes
choice_d: Keep the brakes applied continuously for the entire downgrade
explanation: The manual's example states that if your safe speed is 40 mph, you would apply the brakes hard enough to gradually reduce your speed to 35 mph (about 5 mph below safe speed) and then release the brakes, repeating this as often as necessary until reaching the end of the downgrade, as brakes on a downgrade only supplement the engine's braking effect.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-9

question: According to the manual, what should you do if the low air pressure warning comes on while driving?
choice_a: Continue driving normally until the spring brakes apply on their own
choice_b: Stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible, since there might be an air leak
choice_c: Immediately accelerate to reach the next exit faster
choice_d: Ignore it if the vehicle is lightly loaded
explanation: The manual instructs that if the low air pressure warning comes on, you should stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible because there might be an air leak; it is much safer to stop while there is enough air in the tanks to use the foot brakes, since the spring brakes do not act on all axles.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-9

question: According to the manual, when should you avoid using the parking brakes, and use wheel chocks instead?
choice_a: Whenever the vehicle is fully loaded
choice_b: Only during daytime driving
choice_c: Only when parked on a hill
choice_d: When the brakes are very hot from a steep grade, or very wet in freezing temperatures
explanation: The manual warns not to use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot (from just coming down a steep grade), since heat can damage them, or if the brakes are very wet in freezing temperatures, since they can freeze and prevent the vehicle from moving; use wheel chocks on a level surface instead, and let hot brakes cool or drive lightly in a low gear to dry wet brakes.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-9

question: According to the manual, if your vehicle does not have automatic air tank drains, when should you drain the air tanks?
choice_a: At the end of each working day
choice_b: Once a month
choice_c: Only before long trips
choice_d: Draining is never necessary if the alcohol evaporator is full
explanation: The manual states that if your vehicle does not have automatic air tank drains, you must drain your air tanks at the end of each working day to remove moisture and oil, otherwise the brakes could fail.
source_note: Arizona Commercial Driver License Manual (AAMVA 2005/2022 CDL Testing System, ADOT MVD, Revised 01/2026), Section 5 - Air Brakes, p. 5-10
